title: Frobenius-equivariant rational finite-fibre base change
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, an algebraic closure $k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $g_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a finite etale morphism of finite-type $k_0$-schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism], let $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, $g=g_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $\mathcal F$ be a constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf on $X_0$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex, def-weil-constructible-heart]. Use the rational/common-stage direct image $Rg_*$ of [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. The object $Rg_*\mathcal F$ is concentrated in degree zero, and its degree-zero sheaf $g_*\mathcal F$ is constructible with the Weil structure induced by direct image of that of $\mathcal F$.

Let $y$ be a closed point of $Y_0$, write $L=\kappa(y)$ and $d_y=[L:k_0]$ [def-weil-point-counts-zeta], choose a $k_0$-embedding $L\hookrightarrow k$, and let $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}k\to Y$ be its geometric lift. Put $Z_0=X_0\times_{Y_0}\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-pc-fibre-product] and $Z=Z_0\times_L k$. Then $Z_0$ is finite over $L$, and restriction of $\mathcal F$ to $Z$ defines a constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf $\mathcal G$ on the $L$-scheme $Z_0$: its Weil structure uses the degree-$d_y$ iterate of the structure on $\mathcal F$ and the canonical geometric-point reparametrization. Here local and global geometric Frobenius use [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace, def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius]. The finite-fibre base-change map is a $\Qlb$-linear isomorphism
$$b_y:(g_*\mathcal F)_{\bar y}\xrightarrow{\sim}H_c^0(Z,\mathcal G),$$
with geometric compact cohomology as in [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], and it satisfies
$$b_y F_y=F_{Z/L} b_y,$$
where $F_{Z/L}$ is geometric Frobenius relative to the finite field $L$ on $H_c^0(Z,\mathcal G)$. These stalks and operators are interpreted at a common finite coefficient-field stage and extended to $\Qlb$.

Closed points $z_0$ of $Z_0$ correspond bijectively to the points $x$ of $X_0$ above $y$; those $x$ are closed, and $\kappa(z_0)=\kappa(x)$ as extensions of $L$. For every geometric lift of $z_0$, the restriction map identifies the stalk of $\mathcal G$ with the stalk of $\mathcal F$ at the corresponding lift of $x$, and carries its local geometric-Frobenius operator relative to $L$ to the original $F_x$ relative to $k_0$. No purity, lissity, semisimplicity or surjectivity hypothesis is imposed.

from.place: Proof, first paragraph: application of the finite-stalk formula to rational Weil coefficients, and identification of the local return operator F_x when the fibre is viewed over kappa(y). The finite-fibre cycle decomposition itself is already lem-a1-finite-weil-sections-decomposition.
